summary: @servicetitan/restrict-imports preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated 727KB payload
details: The package's preinstall hook runs `node setup.mjs`, which downloads the Bun runtime from GitHub's oven-sh/bun releases, extracts it to a temp directory, marks it executable, and uses it to execute a sibling file `math_init.js` at install time. `math_init.js` is a 727,680-byte obfuscated JavaScript blob using string-array rotation (`WV8StW` shift routine) and a hex-encoded literal table; its behavior is not inspectable from source. `setup.mjs` itself is obfuscated with `_0xNNNN` mangled identifiers and proxy-object control flow, and fingerprints the host (glibc vs musl via `ldd --version` and Alpine detection via `/etc/os-release`) to select the appropriate Bun binary. The advertised purpose of the package is a static webpack import-restriction plugin, which has no legitimate need for a second language runtime or an obfuscated init payload executed at install. Executing an opaque payload via a downloaded alternate runtime at preinstall runs attacker-chosen code on every installer's machine and evades scanners that only inspect Node-resolved code.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
